translations.en: Sa'd ibn Tariq, al-Hanafi, al-Khaffaf (the boot maker). Narrated from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. Weak.

en.summary: This entry from *Kitab al-Duafa* highlights Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Khaff, a narrator from the generation following the Imams, who transmitted traditions from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, a prominent companion of Imam Ali. His classification as *da'if* (weak) reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied by Shia scholars to ensure the authenticity of chains leading back to the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly given the political and theological complexities of the early Islamic period. en.seo_question: Who is Sa'd ibn Tariq al-Khaffaf and what is his status in hadith sciences?

key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ طَرِيفٍ: Sa'd ibn Tariq, the narrator's name
key_terms.الْحَنْظَلِيُّ: Al-Hanafi, a nisba indicating lineage or tribe
key_terms.الْخَفَّافُ: Al-Khaffaf, meaning the boot maker, a common identifier for narrators
key_terms.الْأَصْبَغُ بْنُ نُبَاتَةَ: Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, the source from whom Sa'd narrated
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating lower reliability
